bio_en: Sahak Sarukhanian, called Sev ('Black') Sahak, was born in 1888 into a modest peasant family in the village of Ghalasar in Salmast and grew up in the atmosphere of the Armenian national awakening there. After the parish school he threw himself into local revolutionary work and took part in the Persian revolutionary movement of 1908. From 1914, as Kurdish attacks grew, he kept his rifle in hand until the Salmast-Urmia self-defence battles of 1918, then shared a year of refugee life. In 1921 he served as a squad leader among the Armenian volunteers the Persian government raised to retake Salmast and Somay from Simko, and he died in 1932.
